clue.text: Having deal, maybe, that's awkward

blocks.note: first meaning: made of wood, deal being one kind of timber
second meaning: stiff and clumsy in manner

explanation.walkthrough: Deal here is not a bargain or a hand of cards but pine or fir board, so having it means being made of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff, clumsy performer is called wooden, so the adjective covers both timber construction and gauche movement.

clue.text: Aim of UN given spin by newspaper article

blocks.note: whirled means spun round
a piece is an article in a paper

explanation.surface: The United Nations' goal distorted by a slanted press report.
explanation.walkthrough: WHIRLED PIECE is a pun: said aloud it is world peace, the definition, while its spelling comes from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping international peace and security is the founding purpose in the United Nations Charter.

clue.text: See 18
Once I am worked out, there may be songs of praise

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: these three words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer saying hymns will follow once their routine is sorted.
explanation.walkthrough: Songs of Praise is also a long-running BBC hymn programme, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Encomia is the plural of encomium, a formal speech or poem of high praise.

clue.text: See 20 down
Achievement with setting up of iron citadel

indicators.note: in a down clue setting something up turns it bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a fort is a fortified stronghold

explanation.surface: An engineering feat: putting up an iron fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort can mean the thing produced by trying, as in a fine effort, so it stands for an accomplishment.

clue.text: We hear satisfied woman-devouring Cockney cannibal is a fighter!

indicators.note: signals that the pieces are judged by their spoken sound

blocks.note: a satisfied cannibal who has eaten a woman says glad I ate her, and a Cockney drops the H of her

explanation.surface: A lurid news line about a contented Londoner who has eaten a woman and turned out to be a warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: Glad I ate 'er, with the dropped H of Cockney speech, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladiators were armed men who fought in Roman arenas, the archetypal fighters.

clue.text: Your unblocked nose's muddled in respect of smell?

indicators.note: the middle block of the word is cleared out, leaving its ends
the letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: YOUR provides its outer letters
the possessive gives the word plus S

explanation.surface: Someone with a clear nose finding their sense of smell confused.
explanation.walkthrough: YR is also the standard short form of your. The question mark admits that smell is only one example of the senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensory means relating to the senses, of which smell is one, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Strange girl and boy, weird to you and me

blocks.note: miss is a word for a girl
Ed is a boy's name
eerie means uncannily strange
US is the pair of you and me

explanation.surface: An odd pair of children who seem uncanny to the rest of us.
explanation.walkthrough: MISSED EERIE US is a pun: said aloud it is mysterious, the definition, while its spelling comes from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysterious means puzzling and hard to explain, which is a sense of strange.

clue.text: Son of Abraham lacking a new sort of coat?

indicators.note: the son's name is shown without the letters that follow, so they are taken out of it

blocks.note: Midian was a son of Abraham by Keturah (Genesis 25)
taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a biblical figure who has lost something and ends up as a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: Isaac and Ishmael are the sons who come to mind first, but neither works; the lesser-known Midian loses A and N from his end.
explanation.definitionFit: A midi is a garment cut to mid-calf length, so a midi coat is one style of overcoat; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: That is newspaper with restrictions about leaders

indicators.note: the restrictions go around the other pieces, so these words signal one thing placed inside another

blocks.note: chains are restraints
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A complaint that the press is muzzled by curbs on its editorials.
explanation.walkthrough: In a newspaper, leaders are editorials, which the surface leans on; in the answer they are heads of clans.
explanation.definitionFit: Chieftains are the heads of tribes or clans, so they are leaders in the plain sense of people in command.

clue.text: Look into defeat in race

indicators.note: the look is put into the defeat, so this word signals placing one piece inside the other

blocks.note: to slam is to beat soundly
LO is the old word for look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: An inquiry into why someone lost a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A slalom is a downhill ski race weaving between gates, so it is one kind of race.

clue.text: English town, second to the city of Rome when leading the fashion

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come in front of the fashion, so these words fix the order of the parts

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
URBI is Latin for to the city, as in the papal blessing urbi et orbi
the ton is an old word for fashionable society or the prevailing mode

explanation.surface: A boast that some English town ranks just behind Rome as a leader of style.
explanation.walkthrough: Urbi et orbi, to the city and the world, is the Pope's blessing to Rome; urbi alone means to the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Surbiton is a suburban town in south-west London, historically part of Surrey.

clue.text: Those who could work for the devil sin had led astray

definitions.text: Those who could work for the devil

indicators.note: words led astray are pulled out of their proper order and rearranged

blocks.note: these three words supply the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sermon line about people whose sin led them off the right path into the devil's service.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs: the devil finds work for idle hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says Satan finds employment for those with nothing to do, so the unoccupied are his potential workforce.

clue.text: Just provide endless food

indicators.note: the word for provide loses its final letter

blocks.note: to equip is to furnish or supply
table can mean the food served, as in she keeps a good table

explanation.surface: A plea to simply lay on an unlimited spread.
explanation.walkthrough: Just looks like the adverb meaning merely; it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Equitable means fair and impartial, the sense of just in a just decision.

clue.text: HQ supports invader

blocks.note: stays are props or braces, as in a ship's rigging
the Huns invaded Europe under Attila

explanation.surface: A military command centre that sustains an attacking force.
explanation.walkthrough: The entry STAY SHUN is a pun: said aloud it is station, the definition, while its spelling comes from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A station, such as a police or military station, serves as a headquarters for its area.

clue.text: See 15
Those who hunt flying saucers

indicators.note: the letters are sent flying and land in a new order

blocks.note: this word supplies the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: UFO spotters searching the sky for alien craft.
explanation.walkthrough: SEA CURS is a pun: said aloud it is seekers, the definition, while its spelling comes from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Seekers are people who search for something, and hunting is searching.

clue.text: One can make things hot for someone who is lying

definitions.text: One can make things hot for someone who is lying

blocks.note: sounds like a threat to give someone trouble, as in make it hot for them
suggests a liar, but means a person lying in bed

explanation.walkthrough: Making things hot for a liar suggests punishing them; really the device heats the sheets for someone lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed warmer, such as a warming pan or hot-water bottle, heats the bedclothes before the sleeper gets in.

clue.text: Smashed window of cleric's office

blocks.note: wrecked means destroyed or broken
an oriel is a projecting bay window on an upper floor

explanation.surface: A broken window in the vicar's study.
explanation.walkthrough: WRECKED ORIEL is a pun: said aloud it is rectorial, the definition, while its spelling comes from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Rectorial means relating to a rector, the clergyman in charge of a parish, or to the post he holds.

clue.text: Solemn assurance

blocks.note: first meaning: serious and sincere in manner
second meaning: a pledge or token of what is to come

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a single phrase for an oath, but the two words are separate meanings, the second being the noun earnest, a deposit or token.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective meaning grave and sincere and also a noun for a pledge given as security.

clue.text: Lost folk whose tragic ships finally capsized?

blocks.note: describes people stranded after shipwreck, which is what castaways are

explanation.surface: A lament for a people whose vessels all went down.
explanation.walkthrough: CASTER WEIGHS is a pun: said aloud it is castaways, people left stranded after their ship went down.
explanation.definitionFit: Castaways are shipwrecked people marooned far from help, so they are lost to the world.

clue.text: Singers and actors given allowance — not performing

indicators.note: the performing letters are not there, so they are dropped from the allowance

blocks.note: the cast is the set of actors in a show
a ration is a fixed allowance
on, as in on stage, means performing

explanation.surface: Out-of-work singers and actors drawing a benefit while resting between jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Castrati were male sopranos or altos of the baroque opera stage, so they are a class of singers.

clue.text: Pundit no longer cocky

blocks.note: EX means former
pert means saucy or cheeky

explanation.surface: A commentator who has lost their swagger.
explanation.definitionFit: A pundit is an authority who gives opinions, the same as an expert.

clue.text: See 1
Shocked maiden burst out when hugged by Donald?

indicators.note: burst out says the letters are broken up and rearranged
the Disney character wraps around the jumbled letters, so this signals placing one piece inside another

blocks.note: Donald Duck, the Disney cartoon character
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
the word itself joins the maiden's letter as material for the jumble

explanation.surface: A startled young woman exclaiming as Donald embraces her.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbstruck means so astonished as to be speechless, a strong form of being shocked.

clue.text: Sheep goes to river as possible source of water

blocks.note: a ewe is a female sheep
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A sheep heading down to the river for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug, so it is something water can be poured from.

clue.text: Small island getting sun somewhere in Ireland

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday
Kerry is a county in south-west Ireland

explanation.surface: A little island enjoying sunshine off the Irish coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A skerry is a small rocky islet, a word especially used in Scotland and Ireland.

clue.text: Notice a shorter one's not green

blocks.note: AD is the short form of the answer itself
vert is the heraldic name for green

explanation.surface: A remark that a shortened sign is not painted green.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says the shorter form, AD, lacks the green, VERT, that the full word has; adding the green back gives the notice.
explanation.definitionFit: An advert is a public notice promoting something, so the two words name the same thing.
